figures.caption: FIGURE 1. Heterogeneity of the 12 open-source fNIRS pretraining datasets: The table on the left reports number of subjects, recording duration, median source–detector (S-D) pair count across processed runs, acquisition device, and task type; the matrix on the right portrays the brain-region coverage.

FIGURE 2. Overview of (A) fNIRS pre-processing pipeline, (B) harmonization pipeline of heterogeneous montages, (C) deriving signal and spatio-chromophore token embedding, and (D) masked pretraining and downstream transfer operations of the foundation model.

FIGURE 3. Montage-harmonization results. (A) Aligned source–detector midpoint positions before slotting and shared canonical 10–05 slots after nearest-slot assignment; color denotes the number of pretraining datasets represented at each slot. (B) Representative 3-D RMS alignment (Ferron 2019), 2-D anchored placement (Defenderfer 2019), and direct label assignment (Ajra 2026); red rings denote slot collisions.

TABLE 2. Benchmark 2 within-subject few-shot. Macro-F1 (%), reported as the mean ± population standard deviation in percentage points across subjects after averaging over 50 repetitions within each subject.

TABLE 3. Few-shot accuracy comparison with prior work on the Gunther 2014 dataset. Prior work values in this table are reproduced from corresponding publications. For MtReNIRS, values are mean ± population standard deviation across subjects after averaging 50 random-seed repetitions within each subject; Highest values are shown in bold.

FIGURE 4. Within-subject few-shot macro-F1 performance across the three held-out evaluation datasets. The plots show the mean and standard deviation across subjects after averaging 50 random-seed repetitions within each subject; colored markers report paired two-sided Wilcoxon tests.
